html:
SMTO-WEB-0014 — The Web search settings have a mistake

GUID: c93af2ce-d400-4b41-b7d5-fba4c6cc004a
Slug: web-configuration-invalid
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't accept the Web search settings because a provider entry has a problem, such as a bad address or name, or the default provider isn't turned on. The settings weren't used.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Capabilities and select Configure Web. For each provider, check the Base URL is a plain http:// or https:// address with nothing after a ? or #. Provider addresses can't contain extra search text, a # part or a username and password.
  2. Make sure each provider's Name is filled in with ordinary text, and its Timeout (seconds) is between 1 and 30. Empty or unusual names and out-of-range timeouts are refused.
  3. Make sure the provider chosen in Default provider is Enabled, or clear the default, then select Save. SMTO won't silently switch to another provider when the chosen default is turned off.
  4. Leave API key (Brave Search only) empty for SearXNG and DuckDuckGo providers, and remove any duplicate provider entry with Remove. Only Brave Search uses a key, and each provider entry must be unique.

What success looks like

  • Save succeeds and Configure Web shows Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't guess the provider type, and don't paste keys or passwords into names or addresses when sharing the settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Web provider configuration failed validation: a provider name, ID, type, URL, settings field or bound is invalid, provider IDs are duplicated, or the default does not name an enabled provider.

What this means

  • Provider configuration rejects invalid names, duplicate IDs, unsupported fields, malformed base URLs or a default that is not enabled. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • Provider configuration rejects invalid names, duplicate IDs, unsupported fields, malformed base URLs or a default that is not enabled.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the field-specific validation result and exact provider IDs instead of testing a guessed fallback.

How to fix it

  • canonicalize in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/models.py validates WebConfiguration strictly (extra fields forbidden): unique provider_id matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$, control-free names up to 80 chars, adapter settings (credential-free base_url without query or fragment, timeout_seconds 1-30, SearXNG api_key null), and a default_provider_id that names an enabled instance or null. Correct the offending entry in the Web Skill configuration and save; do not log credential references.
  • Review the Web skill provider configuration. Use unique IDs, control-free names, supported provider types and base URLs without query strings or fragments; select an enabled default.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported configuration validates and selects the intended enabled provider.

What not to do

  • Do not save a guessed provider type or expose credentials in configuration diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
